item.name: Auth
item.description: Cookie + bearer authentication. Login and register return `{user, accessToken}` and set the `rt` refresh cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/api/v1/auth). Postman stores it in its cookie jar and sends it to `/auth/refresh` and `/auth/logout` automatically; scripts never read it. Those two routes also need `X-Requested-With` (CSRF guard for non-browser clients). The jar holds one `rt` per host, so the most recent login owns it.

request.description:
**LOCAL TESTING ONLY.** Builds a `payment_intent.succeeded` event and signs it with `stripeWebhookSecret` (the `whsec_…` your local server uses, e.g. from `stripe listen`). This stands in for Stripe calling the webhook after a successful card payment. The server still verifies the signature, deduplicates by event id, checks the amount against the order total and fulfills the order. Skips itself unless `baseUrl` is localhost and `stripeWebhookSecret` is set. The server also calls Stripe to read the card details, so the local server needs real Stripe **test** keys. For a real end-to-end payment, confirm the PaymentIntent with the Stripe CLI instead (see the README).

**Access:** Public
